question.text: Registration of a new Portfolio Manager takes place under:

answer.text: SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, with application to SEBI and grant of a certificate of registration

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, no person can act as a portfolio manager unless granted a certificate of registration by SEBI under the SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations. An applicant makes the application in the prescribed format, SEBI considers it under the regulations, and grants the certificate subject to conditions. The Trap: Incorporation under the Companies Act is a pre-requisite for being a body corporate but does not itself authorise acting as a portfolio manager. RBI approval is not the relevant regulator here, and stock-exchange listing has no role in PM registration. Note: Two ideas to remember from the workbook: (i) registration is granted by SEBI under the PM Regulations, and (ii) the certificate is granted on consideration of the application and subject to specified conditions.
